title: Bristol City vs. Wrexham: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich Fay8:00 PM ESTBristol City have lost six of their eight home matches this season. / Visionhaus/Getty Images (Bristol City), Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images (Wrexham)Wrexham will hit the road again when they travel to Bristol City in the Championship on Tuesday.

Phil Parkinson's side head into the match full of confidence following their weekend win over Lincoln, which extended their unbeaten run to three matches and secured just their second away victory of the season.

Bristol City, meanwhile, have lost their previous three matches and their last four at home, including a 5-0 hammering by Norwich the last time they played at Ashton Gate. They will be desperate to put things right in midweek as pressure mounts on manager Michael Skubala.

Wrexham dug deep to keep a clean sheet against Lincoln City at the weekend. / Chris Vaughan/Getty ImagesWrexham only climbed one place in the table after their weekend victory and could move into the top half if they secure another away win midweek. The Red Dragons will find it tough to go again after their hard-fought victory at Lincoln, though, so there would be no shame in taking a point from this match.
Skubala is under increasing pressure at Bristol City, and another disappointing performance and result against Wrexham could bring him closer to the exit.

Bristol City fans hope to see Scott Twine recalled against Wrexham. / FotMobSkubala will have to make changes to his starting lineup in midweek, and the return of Scott Twine would be a hugely popular decision among supporters. The defense should remain unchanged, with the expected alterations coming in attack.
Laurent Tolaj cut a frustrated figure in the weekend defeat to Middlesbrough and could be replaced by Dom Ballard, while Brian De Keersmaecker could also lose his place.
Bristol City predicted lineup (4-2-3-1): Collins; Tanner, Dickie, Atkinson, Pring; Knight, Randell; Cardines, Twine, Hirakawa; Ballard.

Phil Parkinson will refresh his starting lineup in midweek. / FotMobParkinson could also make a change to his starting lineup, with Jacques Ekomié set to return at left wingback after coming off the bench at the weekend. The defense should remain unchanged, with George Thomason moving into central midfield to replace Ollie Rathbone.
The main selection debate is whether Issa Kaboré or Danny Imray starts at right wingback, with Lewis O'Brien expected to play behind Kieffer Moore in attack.
Wrexham predicted lineup (3-5-1-1): Patterson; Cleworth, Worrall, Doyle; Kaboré, Dobson, Whiteman, Thomason, Ekomié; O'Brien; Moore.
